courses.title: Management Principles and Practice, BBA Semester 1

topics.title: Management: concept, functions and skills
topics.summary: Meaning and nature of management, managerial roles and skills.
notes: Management is a process of planning, organising, staffing, directing and controlling to achieve goals efficiently and effectively.
Efficiency is doing things right (minimum resources); effectiveness is doing the right things (achieving goals).
Mintzberg's managerial roles: interpersonal, informational, decisional.
Katz's skills: technical (lower levels), human (all levels), conceptual (top level).
outcomes: Explain the functions and roles of a manager
Relate managerial skills to levels of management

topics.title: Classical, behavioural and modern approaches
topics.summary: Scientific management, administrative theory, bureaucracy, Hawthorne studies and systems and contingency approaches.
notes: Taylor's scientific management: science not rule of thumb, harmony, cooperation, maximum output, development of workers.
Fayol's 14 principles include division of work, authority and responsibility, unity of command, unity of direction, scalar chain and equity.
Max Weber's bureaucracy: hierarchy, rules, impersonality, merit-based appointment.
The Hawthorne studies (Elton Mayo) showed social factors affect productivity; systems and contingency approaches see the organisation as open and its best practice as situational.
outcomes: Apply Fayol's principles to a case

topics.title: Planning, objectives and decisions
topics.summary: Types of plans, steps in planning, MBO and decision-making models.
notes: Strategic plans are long-term and set by top management; tactical plans by middle managers; operational plans for day-to-day work.
SMART objectives are specific, measurable, achievable, relevant and time-bound.
Programmed decisions handle routine problems; non-programmed decisions handle new, unstructured ones.
Simon's bounded rationality: managers "satisfice" rather than optimise.

topics.title: Structure, authority and delegation
topics.summary: Organisation design, centralisation and delegation.
notes: Departmentation by function, product, territory, customer or process.
A narrow span of control creates a tall structure; a wide span a flat one.
Centralisation keeps decision authority at the top; decentralisation spreads it systematically.
Authority can be delegated but accountability cannot.
outcomes: Design a structure for a growing firm

topics.title: Communication, coordination and control
topics.summary: Communication process and barriers, coordination and the control process.
notes: Communication process: sender, encoding, message, channel, decoding, receiver, feedback.
Barriers: semantic, psychological, organisational and physical.
Coordination is the essence of management: it synchronises group efforts.
Control process: set standards, measure, compare, correct; feedforward control acts before problems occur.

courses.title: Fundamentals of Business Accounting, BBA Semester 1

topics.title: Accounting principles and the accounting equation
topics.summary: Meaning, users and branches of accounting, and the accounting equation.
notes: Users: owners, managers, creditors, investors, employees, government.
Branches: financial, cost, management and tax accounting.
Accounting equation: Assets = Liabilities + Capital; every transaction keeps it balanced.
Golden rules: personal — debit the receiver, credit the giver; real — debit what comes in, credit what goes out; nominal — debit expenses and losses, credit incomes and gains.
outcomes: Apply the accounting equation to transactions
Classify accounts and apply the golden rules

lesson.hook: You start a business with ₹50,000 and buy goods for ₹20,000 on credit. What do you own and what do you owe?
lesson.example:
Capital ₹50,000: Assets (cash) 50,000 = Capital 50,000.
Goods ₹20,000 on credit: Assets 70,000 = Liabilities 20,000 + Capital 50,000.

questions.q: Which account is debited when rent is paid?

topics.title: Recording and posting
topics.summary: Journal entries, subsidiary books, ledger posting and the trial balance.
notes: The journal is the book of original entry; entries are posted to ledger accounts and balanced.
Subsidiary books: purchases, sales, returns, cash book, bills books and the journal proper.
A trial balance lists ledger balances; equal totals show arithmetical accuracy but not the absence of all errors.
Errors not disclosed by a trial balance: omission, commission (some), principle and compensating errors.
outcomes: Journalise transactions and post them to the ledger

topics.title: Bank reconciliation
topics.summary: Reasons for differences between cash book and pass book and the reconciliation statement.
notes: Causes: cheques issued but not presented, cheques deposited but not cleared, bank charges, interest and direct credits or debits not yet in the cash book.
Starting from the cash book (debit) balance: add cheques issued but not presented; deduct cheques deposited but not cleared.
An overdraft is a credit balance in the cash book.

lesson.example:
Cash book balance ₹25,000; cheques issued not presented ₹4,000; deposited not cleared ₹6,000; bank charges ₹200.
Pass book balance = 25,000 + 4,000 − 6,000 − 200 = ₹22,800.

topics.title: Trading and profit and loss account and balance sheet
topics.summary: Preparing final accounts with adjustments.
notes: Gross profit = Net sales − Cost of goods sold (Opening stock + Purchases + Direct expenses − Closing stock).
Common adjustments: closing stock, outstanding and prepaid expenses, accrued and advance income, depreciation, bad debts and provision for doubtful debts.
Each adjustment is recorded twice: once in the trading or profit and loss account and once in the balance sheet.
outcomes: Treat outstanding and prepaid items correctly

topics.title: Methods of depreciation
topics.summary: Causes of depreciation and the straight-line and written-down value methods.
notes: Depreciation is the allocation of the depreciable amount of an asset over its useful life.
Straight-line: annual depreciation = (Cost − Residual value) ÷ Useful life.
Written-down value: a fixed rate on the opening book value; the charge falls each year.
Profit or loss on sale = Sale price − Book value on the date of sale.
outcomes: Prepare an asset account with a sale

topics.title: Nature and scope of business economics
topics.summary: Micro and macro economics, and economics for managerial decisions.
notes: Business economics applies economic theory to business decisions: demand, cost, pricing, investment.
Microeconomics studies individual units; macroeconomics studies the economy as a whole.
Basic problems: what, how and for whom to produce, arising from scarcity.
Opportunity cost is the value of the next best alternative forgone.
outcomes: Explain the scope of business economics

topics.title: Demand and elasticity
topics.summary: Law of demand, determinants, and price, income and cross elasticity.
notes: Law of demand: other things equal, quantity demanded rises as price falls.
Price elasticity Ep = % change in quantity demanded ÷ % change in price; elastic if |Ep| > 1.
If demand is elastic, a price cut raises total revenue; if inelastic, it lowers it.
Income elasticity is negative for inferior goods; cross elasticity is positive for substitutes and negative for complements.

lesson.hook: Petrol prices rise 10% but people buy almost as much. Mangoes rise 10% and sales collapse. Why?
lesson.example: Price rises from ₹10 to ₹12 (20%); quantity falls from 100 to 70 (30%). Ep = 30 ÷ 20 = 1.5: elastic.

questions.q: If Ep = 0.4 and price rises, what happens to total revenue?
questions.a: It rises, because demand is inelastic.

topics.title: Production function and costs
topics.summary: Laws of variable proportions, returns to scale and cost curves.
notes: Law of variable proportions: as more of a variable input is added to fixed inputs, marginal product eventually falls.
Returns to scale (all inputs varied): increasing, constant or decreasing.
Total cost = Fixed cost + Variable cost; marginal cost = change in total cost from one more unit.
Short-run average and marginal cost curves are U-shaped; MC cuts AC at its minimum.
outcomes: Explain the law of variable proportions
Derive cost curves from cost data

topics.title: Pricing under different markets
topics.summary: Perfect competition, monopoly, monopolistic competition and oligopoly.
notes: Profit is maximised where MR = MC (and MC cuts MR from below).
Perfect competition: many firms, homogeneous product, price takers (P = MR = AR).
Monopoly: single seller, price maker; may practise price discrimination.
Monopolistic competition: differentiated products and selling costs; oligopoly: few interdependent firms (kinked demand curve).

topics.title: National income and inflation
topics.summary: Concepts and measurement of national income, and inflation.
notes: GDP is the market value of final goods and services produced within a country in a year.
Methods: product (value added), income and expenditure (C + I + G + (X − M)).
Inflation is a sustained rise in the general price level; India's RBI targets 4% CPI inflation (±2%).
Business cycle phases: expansion, peak, recession, trough.
outcomes: Explain the causes and effects of inflation

courses.title: Financial Accounting and Reporting, BBA Semester 2

topics.title: Accounting standards in India
topics.summary: AS, Ind AS and IFRS convergence.
notes: Ind AS (notified under the Companies Act) are converged with IFRS; they apply in phases to listed and large companies.
Other companies follow the Accounting Standards (AS) notified for them.
Key standards: Ind AS 1 (presentation), Ind AS 2 (inventories), Ind AS 16 (property, plant and equipment), Ind AS 115 (revenue).
outcomes: Name key Ind AS and their subjects

topics.title: Issue and forfeiture of shares
topics.summary: Issue at par and premium, calls, forfeiture and reissue.
notes: Securities premium can be used only for purposes in section 52 (e.g. issuing bonus shares, writing off preliminary expenses).
Shares are issued at par or premium; issue at a discount is barred except sweat equity.
On forfeiture, share capital is debited with the called-up amount, and the amount received is credited to share forfeiture.
On reissue, any discount is debited to forfeiture; the balance of forfeiture on reissued shares goes to capital reserve.
outcomes: Pass entries for issue, calls and forfeiture
Compute the transfer to capital reserve on reissue

lesson.example:
100 shares of ₹10 forfeited after ₹6 paid; reissued at ₹8 fully paid.
Forfeiture ₹600; discount on reissue ₹200; capital reserve ₹400.

topics.title: Financial statements under Schedule III
topics.summary: Balance sheet and statement of profit and loss of a company.
notes: Schedule III (Division I for AS, Division II for Ind AS) prescribes the format.
Equity and liabilities: shareholders' funds, non-current liabilities, current liabilities.
Statement of profit and loss shows revenue from operations, other income, expenses, tax and profit for the period.
outcomes: Prepare a company balance sheet with notes
Classify items in the Schedule III format

topics.title: Annual report and corporate reporting
topics.summary: Contents of the annual report and recent reporting trends.
notes: The annual report contains the directors' report, auditor's report, financial statements and notes, and management discussion and analysis.
Listed companies publish a Business Responsibility and Sustainability Report (BRSR).
Integrated reporting combines financial and non-financial (environmental, social, governance) information.
outcomes: Read the main parts of an annual report

topics.title: Nature and models of OB
topics.summary: Meaning, levels and models of organisational behaviour.
notes: OB studies how individuals, groups and structure affect behaviour in organisations.
Levels of analysis: individual, group, organisation.
Models of OB: autocratic, custodial, supportive, collegial.

topics.title: Personality, perception and learning
topics.summary: Determinants of personality, the perception process and learning theories.
notes: Big Five personality traits: openness, conscientiousness, extraversion, agreeableness, neuroticism.
Perception errors: stereotyping, halo effect, selective perception, projection.
Learning theories: classical conditioning, operant conditioning (reinforcement), social learning.

topics.title: Attitudes and motivation
topics.summary: Job satisfaction, attitudes and process theories of motivation.
notes: Attitudes have cognitive, affective and behavioural components.
Vroom's expectancy theory: Motivation = Expectancy × Instrumentality × Valence.
Adams' equity theory: people compare their output–input ratio with others'.

topics.title: Groups and teams
topics.summary: Group formation, team types and group decision making.
notes: Tuckman's stages: forming, storming, norming, performing, adjourning.
Groupthink is pressure for conformity that suppresses dissent.
Team types: problem-solving, self-managed, cross-functional, virtual.

topics.title: Conflict, stress and change
topics.summary: Conflict management styles, stress and Lewin's change model.
notes: Thomas–Kilmann conflict styles: competing, collaborating, compromising, avoiding, accommodating.
Stressors may be environmental, organisational or individual.
Lewin's model of change: unfreeze, change (move), refreeze; resistance arises from habit, fear and self-interest.
outcomes: Choose a conflict style for a situation
Plan a change using Lewin's model

topics.title: Ratios, proportions and equations
topics.summary: Ratio, proportion, percentages and solving linear and quadratic equations.
notes: If a : b = c : d then ad = bc.
Quadratic ax² + bx + c = 0: x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac)) ÷ 2a.
Simultaneous linear equations can be solved by substitution, elimination or matrices.
outcomes: Use ratios to share profits and costs

topics.title: Interest, discount and annuities
topics.summary: Simple and compound interest, discounting bills and annuities.
notes: True discount = Amount × r × t ÷ (100 + r × t); banker's discount = Amount × r × t ÷ 100.
Present value of an annuity = A[1 − (1 + i)⁻ⁿ] ÷ i.

topics.title: Matrices and determinants
topics.summary: Matrix algebra and solving equations by the inverse method.
notes: A matrix is invertible only if its determinant is non-zero.
A⁻¹ = adj A ÷ |A|.
AX = B gives X = A⁻¹B.
outcomes: Find the inverse of a 3 × 3 matrix

topics.title: Arithmetic and geometric progressions
topics.summary: nth term and sum of AP and GP, and logarithms.
notes: GP: tₙ = arⁿ⁻¹; Sₙ = a(rⁿ − 1) ÷ (r − 1), r ≠ 1.
log(mn) = log m + log n; log(m/n) = log m − log n; log mⁿ = n log m.

topics.title: Formulating and solving LPP graphically
topics.summary: Objective function, constraints and the graphical method.
notes: An LPP maximises or minimises a linear objective function subject to linear constraints and non-negativity.
The feasible region is the set of points satisfying all constraints.
The optimum lies at a corner point of the feasible region.
outcomes: Formulate an LPP from a business problem

topics.title: Cost concepts and cost sheet
topics.summary: Cost objects, cost centres, classification and the cost sheet.
notes: A cost centre is a location or activity for which costs are collected; a cost unit is the unit of output costed.
Costs by behaviour: fixed, variable, semi-variable; by traceability: direct and indirect.
Cost sheet: prime cost, works cost, cost of production, cost of sales, profit.

lesson.example: Materials 50,000 + labour 30,000 + direct expenses 5,000 = prime cost ₹85,000; works overheads 15,000: works cost ₹1,00,000.

topics.title: Inventory control techniques
topics.summary: EOQ, stock levels and ABC analysis.
notes: EOQ = √(2AO ÷ C).
ABC analysis: A items (high value, few) get tight control; C items (low value, many) simple control.
JIT aims to keep minimal inventory by receiving goods only as needed.

topics.title: Wage systems and incentives
topics.summary: Time and piece wages, idle time and overtime.
notes: Normal idle time is part of labour cost; abnormal idle time goes to costing profit and loss.
Halsey bonus = 50% of time saved × rate; Rowan bonus = time taken ÷ time allowed × time saved × rate.
Overtime premium is charged to the job only if overtime was at the customer's request.
outcomes: Treat idle time and overtime correctly

topics.title: Overhead distribution and absorption
topics.summary: Allocation, apportionment and absorption rates.
notes: Apportion common overheads on fair bases (area, horsepower, value of assets, number of workers).
Service department costs are redistributed to production departments.
Absorption rate = Budgeted overheads ÷ Budgeted base (machine hours, labour hours).

topics.title: CVP analysis
topics.summary: Contribution, P/V ratio, break-even and decision making.
notes: BEP (units) = Fixed cost ÷ Contribution per unit.
Sales for target profit = (Fixed cost + Target profit) ÷ P/V ratio.
With a limiting factor, rank products by contribution per unit of the limiting factor.
outcomes: Compute break-even point and margin of safety
Make a make-or-buy decision with marginal costing

courses.title: Statistics for Business Decisions, BBA Semester 3

topics.title: Data, classification and diagrams
topics.summary: Primary and secondary data, frequency distributions and charts.
notes: Primary data is collected first-hand (surveys, interviews); secondary data from published sources.
Class width = upper limit − lower limit; class mark = (lower + upper) ÷ 2.
Diagrams: bar, pie; graphs: histogram, frequency polygon, ogive (cumulative frequency curve).

topics.title: Averages and spread
topics.summary: Mean, median, mode, standard deviation and coefficient of variation.
notes: x̄ = Σfx ÷ N; median = L + ((N/2 − cf) ÷ f) × h.
σ = √(Σfd² ÷ N − (Σfd ÷ N)²) × h by the step-deviation method.

lesson.hook: Two salespeople both average ₹1 lakh a month. Who is more reliable?
lesson.example: A: σ = ₹10,000, CV 10%; B: σ = ₹30,000, CV 30%. A is more consistent.

questions.q: Which average is best for data with extreme values?

topics.title: Skewness and kurtosis
topics.summary: Measures of the shape of a distribution.
notes: Karl Pearson's coefficient of skewness = (Mean − Mode) ÷ σ, or 3(Mean − Median) ÷ σ.
Bowley's coefficient = (Q₃ + Q₁ − 2 Median) ÷ (Q₃ − Q₁).
Positive skew: mean > median > mode; kurtosis measures peakedness (normal β₂ = 3).
outcomes: Compute Karl Pearson's and Bowley's coefficients

topics.title: Correlation and regression for business
topics.summary: Measuring and using relationships between variables.
notes: r ranges from −1 to +1; r² is the proportion of variation explained.
Regression of y on x predicts y from x; byx = r σy ÷ σx.
Spearman's R = 1 − 6Σd² ÷ n(n² − 1).

topics.title: Index numbers and trends
topics.summary: Weighted index numbers and trend fitting.
notes: Laspeyres uses base-year quantities; Paasche current-year quantities; Fisher is their geometric mean.
Deflating: real value = money value ÷ price index × 100.
Trend by least squares: y = a + bx.

topics.title: Core marketing concepts
topics.summary: Needs, value, exchange, and the holistic marketing concept.
notes: Customer value = Perceived benefits − Perceived costs.
Holistic marketing: relationship, integrated, internal and performance (socially responsible) marketing.
Customer lifetime value is the present value of profits from a customer over the relationship.
outcomes: Explain the core concepts of marketing
Compute a simple customer lifetime value

topics.title: Consumer behaviour and STP
topics.summary: Factors influencing buying, and segmentation, targeting and positioning.
notes: Influences: cultural, social, personal and psychological factors.
Effective segments are measurable, substantial, accessible, differentiable and actionable.
Positioning is built on points of difference and points of parity.

topics.title: Product strategy and pricing
topics.summary: Product mix, new product development, PLC and pricing strategies.
notes: Product mix has width (lines), length (items), depth (variants) and consistency.
New product development: idea generation, screening, concept testing, business analysis, product development, test marketing, commercialisation.
Pricing: skimming, penetration, psychological, bundle and dynamic pricing.

topics.title: Channels and integrated marketing communication
topics.summary: Channel design and the promotion mix.
notes: Intensive, selective or exclusive distribution.
IMC coordinates advertising, sales promotion, PR, personal selling, direct and digital marketing.
Push strategy promotes to intermediaries; pull strategy to final consumers.

topics.title: Digital, rural and green marketing
topics.summary: Digital marketing, the rural market in India and sustainable marketing.
notes: Digital marketing metrics: reach, click-through rate (clicks ÷ impressions), conversion rate, cost per acquisition.
Rural marketing challenges: dispersed markets, low incomes, poor infrastructure; the 4 As: availability, affordability, acceptability, awareness.
Green marketing promotes environmentally safe products; greenwashing is false environmental claims.
outcomes: Plan for rural markets with the 4 As

topics.title: Finance function and goals
topics.summary: Investment, financing and dividend decisions and wealth maximisation.
notes: The finance manager raises funds, invests them and decides on dividends.
Shareholder wealth maximisation considers timing and risk of returns.
Risk and return: higher expected return comes with higher risk.

topics.title: Compounding and discounting
topics.summary: Future and present values of sums and annuities.
notes: FV = PV(1 + r)ⁿ; PV = FV ÷ (1 + r)ⁿ.
PV of an annuity = A[1 − (1 + r)⁻ⁿ] ÷ r; perpetuity PV = A ÷ r.
Effective rate = (1 + r/m)^m − 1.

lesson.hook: A lottery offers ₹10 lakh today or ₹1 lakh a year for 15 years. Which is worth more at 8%?

questions.q: PV of ₹5,000 a year forever at 10%?

topics.title: Capital budgeting
topics.summary: Payback, NPV, IRR and profitability index.
notes: NPV = Σ CFₜ ÷ (1 + k)ᵗ − Initial outlay.
IRR: the discount rate that makes NPV zero.
Payback ignores cash flows after the payback period and the time value of money (discounted payback fixes the latter).
outcomes: Evaluate projects using NPV and IRR

topics.title: Cost of capital and leverage
topics.summary: Specific costs, WACC, and operating and financial leverage.
notes: Kd = I(1 − t) ÷ NP; Ke = D₁ ÷ P₀ + g (or by CAPM: Rf + β(Rm − Rf)).
WACC weights each source by its proportion in the capital structure.
DOL = Contribution ÷ EBIT; DFL = EBIT ÷ EBT.

topics.title: Managing working capital
topics.summary: Operating cycle, financing and cash management.
notes: Gross working capital = Current assets; net working capital = Current assets − Current liabilities.
Operating cycle = Inventory period + Receivables period − Payables period.
Baumol's model: optimal cash balance C = √(2bT ÷ i).

topics.title: HRM and strategic HRM
topics.summary: Functions of HRM and aligning HR with strategy.
notes: HRM functions: acquisition, development, motivation and maintenance of people.
Strategic HRM aligns HR practices with business strategy.
HR metrics: attrition rate, cost per hire, time to fill, training ROI.

topics.title: Job analysis, recruitment and selection
topics.summary: Job description and specification, recruitment sources and selection tests.
notes: Job analysis methods: observation, interview, questionnaire.
Selection tests: aptitude, personality, interest, achievement; interviews may be structured or unstructured.
Reliability is consistency of a test; validity is whether it measures what it should.

topics.title: Training and career development
topics.summary: Training needs analysis, methods and career planning.
notes: Training needs analysis at organisation, task and person levels.
E-learning and simulations scale training at lower cost.
Career planning matches individual goals with organisational opportunities; succession planning prepares replacements.

topics.title: Appraisal and compensation
topics.summary: Appraisal methods, job evaluation and incentives.
notes: 360-degree feedback gathers ratings from supervisors, peers, subordinates and customers.
Job evaluation (ranking, grading, point method) fixes the relative worth of jobs.
Incentives: individual (piece rate, commission) and group (profit sharing, ESOPs).

topics.title: Welfare, safety and discipline
topics.summary: Welfare measures, health and safety, and disciplinary procedure.
notes: Welfare may be statutory (canteens, first aid) or voluntary (housing, education).
Discipline follows natural justice: charge-sheet, show-cause notice, enquiry, decision.
Exit interviews help understand reasons for leaving.

topics.title: Research process and types
topics.summary: Meaning, types and steps of business research.
notes: Types: exploratory, descriptive, causal (experimental); basic and applied.
Research process: define the problem, review literature, form hypotheses, design, collect data, analyse, report.
A hypothesis is a testable statement about the relationship between variables.

topics.title: Sampling methods
topics.summary: Probability and non-probability sampling and sample size.
notes: Probability sampling: simple random, systematic, stratified, cluster.
Non-probability: convenience, judgement, quota, snowball.
Sampling error falls as sample size rises.

topics.title: Questionnaires and scales
topics.summary: Primary data methods, questionnaire design and measurement scales.
notes: Scales: nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio.
A Likert scale measures agreement on (usually) five points.
Good questions are clear, unbiased, single-barrelled and not leading.
outcomes: Identify the scale of a variable

topics.title: Hypothesis testing basics
topics.summary: Null hypothesis, significance and common tests.
notes: Reject H₀ if the p-value < α (e.g. 0.05).
t-test (small samples, means), z-test (large samples), chi-square (association), ANOVA (several means).
Type I error is rejecting a true H₀; its probability is α.
outcomes: Choose a test for a research question

topics.title: Research report
topics.summary: Structure and presentation of a research report.
notes: Structure: title, abstract, introduction, literature review, methodology, analysis, findings, conclusions, references, appendices.
Cite sources consistently (e.g. APA style).
Plagiarism is presenting others' work as one's own.

topics.title: Entrepreneur and entrepreneurship
topics.summary: Concept, traits, types and functions of entrepreneurs.
notes: An entrepreneur identifies opportunities, bears risk and organises resources to create value.
Traits: need for achievement, risk taking, innovation, persistence.
Types: innovative, imitative, Fabian, drone; intrapreneurs innovate inside existing firms.
outcomes: Describe the traits and types of entrepreneurs

topics.title: Opportunity and feasibility analysis
topics.summary: Sources of ideas, screening and the feasibility study.
notes: Sources of ideas: customer problems, trends, technology, hobbies, existing businesses.
Feasibility: market, technical, financial and organisational.
A business model canvas has nine blocks, including customer segments, value proposition, channels and revenue streams.

topics.title: Writing a business plan
topics.summary: Contents of a business plan and project report.
notes: Sections: executive summary, business description, market analysis, marketing plan, operations, management, financial projections.
Financial projections include projected profit and loss, cash flows and break-even.
A pitch deck summarises the plan for investors.

topics.title: Support for entrepreneurs in India
topics.summary: MSMEs, Startup India and financing sources.
notes: MSME classification (from 2025): micro up to ₹2.5 crore investment and ₹10 crore turnover; small up to ₹25 crore and ₹100 crore; medium up to ₹125 crore and ₹500 crore.
Startup India gives recognition, tax benefits (section 80-IAC) and funds of funds.
Funding sources: bootstrapping, angel investors, venture capital, bank loans, MUDRA loans.
outcomes: Identify support schemes for a start-up

courses.title: Production and Operations Management, BBA Semester 5

topics.title: Operations function
topics.summary: Scope of operations management and production systems.
notes: Operations transform inputs into goods and services.
Production systems: job, batch, mass and continuous (process) production.
Productivity = Output ÷ Input.

topics.title: Location and layout
topics.summary: Factors in plant location and types of layout.
notes: Location factors: markets, raw materials, labour, transport, utilities, government incentives.
Layouts: process (functional), product (line), fixed position, cellular.
A product layout suits mass production; a process layout suits varied jobs.
outcomes: Evaluate locations with a factor-rating method

topics.title: Production planning and scheduling
topics.summary: Aggregate planning, routing, scheduling and dispatching.
notes: Production planning and control: routing, scheduling, dispatching, follow-up.
Gantt charts show schedules against time.
Johnson's rule sequences n jobs on two machines to minimise total time.

topics.title: Inventory and quality management
topics.summary: Inventory control, statistical quality control and TQM.
notes: EOQ = √(2DS ÷ H).
Control charts: x̄ and R charts (variables), p and c charts (attributes).
TQM principles: customer focus, continuous improvement (kaizen), employee involvement; Six Sigma targets 3.4 defects per million.

topics.title: Lean, supply chain and maintenance
topics.summary: Lean operations, supply chain management and maintenance.
notes: Lean eliminates waste (muda); JIT and kanban pull production.
A supply chain links suppliers, manufacturers, distributors, retailers and customers; the bullwhip effect amplifies demand swings upstream.
Maintenance: preventive, breakdown, predictive.

topics.title: Strategy and the strategic management process
topics.summary: Vision, mission, objectives and the process of strategic management.
notes: Process: environmental scanning, strategy formulation, implementation, evaluation and control.
Vision is the desired future; mission is the organisation's purpose and scope.
Levels of strategy: corporate, business, functional.

topics.title: SWOT, PESTLE and Porter's five forces
topics.summary: Tools for internal and external analysis.
notes: SWOT: internal strengths and weaknesses, external opportunities and threats.
Porter's five forces: rivalry, threat of new entrants, threat of substitutes, bargaining power of buyers and of suppliers.
Value chain: primary activities (inbound logistics, operations, outbound logistics, marketing and sales, service) and support activities.
outcomes: Do a SWOT and five-forces analysis

topics.title: Corporate and business strategies
topics.summary: Growth, stability and retrenchment, and Porter's generic strategies.
notes: Ansoff matrix: market penetration, market development, product development, diversification.
Porter's generic strategies: cost leadership, differentiation, focus.
BCG matrix: stars, cash cows, question marks, dogs (market growth vs relative share).
outcomes: Classify strategies with Ansoff and BCG

topics.title: Implementing and evaluating strategy
topics.summary: Structure, leadership, culture and the balanced scorecard.
notes: Structure follows strategy (Chandler).
McKinsey 7-S: strategy, structure, systems, shared values, style, staff, skills.
Balanced scorecard perspectives: financial, customer, internal processes, learning and growth.

topics.title: Nature of international business
topics.summary: Drivers of globalisation and modes of entry.
notes: Drivers: market, cost, government and competitive factors.
Entry modes: exporting, licensing, franchising, contract manufacturing, joint ventures, wholly owned subsidiaries.
Risk and control increase from exporting to wholly owned subsidiaries.

topics.title: Theories of international trade
topics.summary: Mercantilism, absolute and comparative advantage, and Porter's diamond.
notes: Absolute advantage (Smith): produce what you make more efficiently than others.
Comparative advantage (Ricardo): specialise where your opportunity cost is lowest; trade benefits both.
Porter's diamond: factor conditions, demand conditions, related industries, firm strategy and rivalry.

topics.title: WTO, IMF and World Bank
topics.summary: Roles of global economic institutions and trade blocs.
notes: WTO principles: most-favoured nation, national treatment, transparency.
The IMF supports balance of payments stability; the World Bank funds development.
Regional blocs: EU, ASEAN, SAARC, USMCA.
outcomes: Explain the role of the WTO
Distinguish IMF and World Bank roles

topics.title: Exchange rates and export procedure
topics.summary: Exchange rate systems, balance of payments and export documents.
notes: Balance of payments: current account (trade, services, transfers) and capital/financial account.
Rupee depreciation makes exports cheaper and imports dearer.
Export documents: commercial invoice, packing list, bill of lading or airway bill, certificate of origin, shipping bill; letters of credit reduce payment risk.
outcomes: Read a balance of payments summary
